sections.text:
Moving House: A Five-Step Checklist

A. If you rent, check your tenancy agreement for the notice period you must give your landlord; in many cases it is a month, but some contracts ask for more. Next, decide whether you will hire a removal firm or move your belongings yourself. Anwar Tasker, who manages a removal company, recommends booking at least four weeks ahead, particularly if you hope to move at the end of a month, when demand is highest. 'Most people want to move on a Friday, so the first slots to disappear are those,' he says. Ask each firm for a written quote and find out whether insurance for breakages is included or costs extra. This is also a good time to sort through cupboards: anything you sell, donate or throw away now is something you will not have to pack, carry or pay to transport.

B. Contact your current energy and water suppliers to tell them the date you are leaving, so that you stop being charged from that day. On the day itself, read every meter at both the old and new property and photograph the figures; a dated image is the simplest way to settle a disagreement about a final bill. Do not assume you must stay with the supplier the previous occupant used. You can usually switch once you have moved in, although it may be worth checking whether any early-exit fee applies to a fixed-term deal at your old address. Broadband deserves special attention, because connecting a new line can take two weeks or longer. Arrange it well in advance if you work from home, and keep your mobile data allowance in mind for the first few days.

C. However carefully you update your address, some letters will still go to your old home. A paid redirection service, offered by the postal service in many countries, forwards your mail to the new address for a chosen period, often three, six or twelve months. Apply at least a week before moving, since the service does not begin immediately. Redirection should be treated as a safety net rather than a solution, however. Write a list of everyone who sends you post — your bank, employer, pension provider, insurers and any magazine subscriptions — and inform each of them directly. Important documents such as bank cards may not be forwarded at all, for security reasons. It is also sensible to leave your new address with a trusted neighbour, who can pass on anything that slips through.

D. Soon after you arrive, contact the local council about any local property tax and, where relevant, waste collection; some areas issue recycling bins only on request. Adding yourself to the electoral register at your new address is a separate step in many places, so do not assume the council will do it automatically. Yolanda Prescott, a housing adviser who has helped hundreds of families relocate, says the step people most often postpone is finding a doctor. 'They wait until a child is ill, and then discover the nearest practice is not taking new patients,' she explains. Her advice is to register as soon as you have the keys, and to look for a dentist at the same time, as waiting lists can be long. Parents should contact the education authority early about school places, which are usually allocated by area.

E. Pack a single box of essentials to travel with you rather than in the van: phone chargers, medicines, a kettle, basic tools, toilet paper and a change of clothes. Before you leave the old property, walk through every room, check cupboards and the loft, and take photographs to show the condition you left it in, which may help if there is a dispute about your deposit. Hand over all keys and get a receipt if possible. In your first week, update the address on your driving licence and vehicle documents; in some countries failing to do so can lead to a fine. Finally, find out where your nearest pharmacy and supermarket are before you need them. Small preparations like these make the first evenings in a new home far less stressful.

questions.prompt: Removal firms usually charge higher prices for moves that take place on a Friday.

explanation.en: Section A says Friday slots are booked first and demand is highest at the end of the month, but it says nothing about whether prices are higher on Fridays.
explanation.ru: В разделе A сказано, что пятничные даты бронируют первыми, а спрос выше всего в конце месяца, но о том, дороже ли переезд в пятницу, ничего не говорится.

questions.prompt: New residents have to remain with the energy supplier chosen by the people who lived there before them.

explanation.en: Section B says you do not have to stay with the previous occupant's supplier and can usually switch after moving in.
explanation.ru: В разделе B сказано, что вы не обязаны оставаться у поставщика, которым пользовался предыдущий жилец, и обычно можете сменить его после заселения.

questions.prompt: It can take more than a fortnight to get a new broadband line working.
questions.evidence: connecting a new line can take two weeks or longer

explanation.en: Section B says connecting a new line can take two weeks or longer; a fortnight means two weeks.
explanation.ru: В разделе B говорится, что подключение новой линии может занять две недели или больше; "fortnight" как раз означает две недели.
explanation.uk: У розділі B сказано, що підключення нової лінії може тривати два тижні або довше; "fortnight" якраз означає два тижні.

questions.prompt: The redirection service costs the same amount whatever length of time you choose.

explanation.en: Section C says the service is paid and lists the usual periods, but it gives no information about whether the price changes with the length of time.
explanation.ru: В разделе C сказано, что услуга платная, и перечислены обычные сроки её действия, но не говорится, меняется ли цена в зависимости от срока.
explanation.uk: У розділі C сказано, що послуга платна, і перелічено звичайні строки її дії, але не сказано, чи змінюється ціна залежно від строку.

questions.prompt: Mail redirection starts on the same day that you apply for it.
questions.evidence: since the service does not begin immediately

explanation.en: Section C tells you to apply at least a week before moving because the service does not start straight away.
explanation.ru: В разделе C советуют подать заявку не позже чем за неделю до переезда, потому что услуга начинает действовать не сразу.
explanation.uk: У розділі C радять подати заявку щонайменше за тиждень до переїзду, бо послуга починає діяти не одразу.

questions.prompt: In some areas, residents only receive recycling bins if they ask for them.

explanation.ru: В разделе D сказано, что в некоторых районах контейнеры для вторсырья выдают только по запросу жителей.
explanation.uk: У розділі D сказано, що в деяких районах контейнери для вторсировини видають лише на запит мешканців.

sections.text:
Team Leaders Wanted at Northgate Distribution

A. Northgate Distribution is looking for eight team leaders to join its regional centre in Halbrook. Over the next year the site will open a new chilled section for fresh food, which means more orders, more vehicles and more people on every shift. Successful applicants will each be responsible for a team of between twelve and fifteen warehouse operatives, working either a day pattern (6 a.m. to 2 p.m.) or a night pattern (10 p.m. to 6 a.m.). Both are permanent, full-time positions, and the starting salary is reviewed after the first six months.

B. So what does the job actually involve? According to site manager Owen Kariuki, it is less about giving orders than people imagine. 'A good team leader isn't someone who walks around with a clipboard,' he says. 'They start every shift with a short briefing, share out the work fairly, keep an eye on accuracy and sort out problems before they grow.' When someone calls in sick or a delivery arrives late, the team leader decides how to move people around so that orders still leave on time. Owen adds that the quality he values most is the ability to stay calm when things go wrong. 'I'd much rather have someone who owns up to a mistake straight away than someone who hides it until the end of the shift.'

C. You do not need to have held the title of supervisor before. We ask for at least one year's experience in a warehouse, retail or delivery setting, along with good spoken and written English and basic computer skills. A forklift licence is useful but not essential, since we can arrange the training. Current Northgate employees are encouraged to apply. Dev Sandoval, who joined as a picker four years ago and now leads the night team in the ambient section, says the biggest adjustment was not the paperwork but the relationships. 'Suddenly I was giving feedback to people I'd been having lunch with the week before. You have to be fair to everyone, including your friends.'

D. New team leaders are not left to work things out alone. Training lead Mirjam Tanaka runs a six-week induction that begins with a fortnight of shadowing, during which each newcomer works alongside an experienced leader on the same shift pattern they will later take over. This is followed by a short course on coaching and handling difficult conversations. 'People often assume the system is the hard part,' Mirjam says, 'but most can learn the stock software in a few days. Listening well takes longer.' Night-shift leaders receive an additional allowance, and all staff have access to a pension scheme and a subsidised canteen.

E. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an assessment day at the Halbrook site. Recruitment coordinator Yara Bellamy explains that it lasts about four hours and has three parts: a guided tour of the warehouse floor, a group exercise and a one-to-one interview. 'Please bring photo ID and proof of your right to work in the UK,' she says. 'For the tour you must wear closed-toe shoes. If you don't own safety boots, tell us your size in advance and we'll lend you a pair.' Candidates who arrive late may not be able to join the tour, because groups leave reception on the hour.

F. In the group exercise, candidates are given a realistic problem, such as planning a shift when three operatives are absent and a large order has just come in. Yara stresses that the assessors are not looking for the loudest voice in the room. 'We notice who listens, who checks that quieter people have had their say, and who keeps an eye on the clock.' Health and safety officer Luka Petrović also sits on the panel. He pays particular attention to whether candidates raise safety without being prompted. 'On the tour, I'm interested in people who spot a blocked fire exit or a pallet stacked too high and mention it. That tells me more than any answer they've rehearsed.'

G. The final interview is usually led by Owen himself. He asks every candidate to describe a real occasion when a plan fell apart and what they did next, so it is worth preparing two or three examples from your own working life. Dev's advice is simple: 'Be honest about what you'd do differently now.' To apply, complete the online form by 28 March. If you need any adjustments for the assessment day, contact Yara directly before you attend.

questions.prompt: Northgate needs more team leaders partly because the Halbrook site is about to add a ______ for fresh food.
questions.evidence: the site will open a new chilled section for fresh food

explanation.en: Paragraph A explains that the site will open a new area for fresh food, the chilled section, which will bring more orders and people.
explanation.ru: В абзаце A объясняется, что на складе откроется новый участок для свежих продуктов — «chilled section», и это принесёт больше заказов и потребует больше людей.
explanation.uk: В абзаці A пояснюється, що на складі відкриється нова ділянка для свіжих продуктів — «chilled section», і це принесе більше замовлень і потребуватиме більше людей.

questions.prompt: At the beginning of each shift, a team leader gives the team a short ______.

explanation.uk: В абзаці B Owen Kariuki каже, що керівники команд починають кожну зміну з короткого інструктажу.

questions.prompt: As well as a year's relevant experience and good English, applicants need basic ______.
questions.evidence: good spoken and written English and basic computer skills

explanation.en: Paragraph C lists the requirements: experience, good spoken and written English, and basic computer skills.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C перечислены требования: опыт работы, хороший устный и письменный английский и базовые навыки работы с компьютером.
explanation.uk: В абзаці C перелічено вимоги: досвід роботи, добра усна й письмова англійська та базові навички роботи з комп’ютером.

questions.prompt: Having a ______ is an advantage, but it is not required because the company can provide the training.
questions.evidence: A forklift licence is useful but not essential, since we can arrange the training

explanation.en: Paragraph C says a forklift licence is useful but not essential. 'An advantage, but not required' restates 'useful but not essential'.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C сказано, что права на погрузчик полезны, но не обязательны. «An advantage, but not required» — это перефразированное «useful but not essential».
explanation.uk: В абзаці C сказано, що посвідчення водія навантажувача корисне, але не обов’язкове. «An advantage, but not required» — це перефразоване «useful but not essential».

questions.prompt: The induction opens with two weeks of ______, when newcomers work next to an experienced leader.
questions.evidence: a six-week induction that begins with a fortnight of shadowing

explanation.en: Paragraph D says the induction begins with a fortnight (two weeks) of shadowing an experienced leader.
explanation.ru: В абзаце D говорится, что вводное обучение начинается с «fortnight» (двух недель), в течение которых новичок работает рядом с опытным руководителем и наблюдает за ним.
explanation.uk: В абзаці D йдеться про те, що вступне навчання починається з «fortnight» (двох тижнів), протягом яких новачок працює поруч із досвідченим керівником і спостерігає за ним.

questions.prompt: Leaders who work nights are paid an extra ______.
questions.evidence: Night-shift leaders receive an additional allowance

explanation.en: Paragraph D states that night-shift leaders receive an additional allowance. The pension and canteen are for all staff, not only night workers.
explanation.ru: В абзаце D указано, что руководители ночных смен получают дополнительную надбавку. Пенсия и столовая положены всем сотрудникам, а не только тем, кто работает ночью.
explanation.uk: В абзаці D зазначено, що керівники нічних змін отримують додаткову надбавку. Пенсія та їдальня передбачені для всіх працівників, а не лише для тих, хто працює вночі.

explanation.en: In paragraph F, Yara Bellamy says the assessors notice who checks that quieter people have had their say, not who is loudest.
explanation.ru: В абзаце F Yara Bellamy говорит, что оценщики обращают внимание на тех, кто следит, чтобы более тихие участники тоже высказались, а не на самых громких.
explanation.uk: В абзаці F Yara Bellamy каже, що оцінювачі звертають увагу на тих, хто стежить, щоб тихіші учасники теж висловилися, а не на найгучніших.

questions.prompt: Interviewees should be open about how they would now handle a past situation in another way.
questions.evidence: Be honest about what you'd do differently now.

explanation.en: In paragraph G, Dev Sandoval advises candidates to be honest about what they would do differently now. Owen asks the question, but this advice comes from Dev.
explanation.ru: В абзаце G Dev Sandoval советует кандидатам честно сказать, что они сделали бы сейчас по-другому. Вопрос задаёт Owen, но этот совет даёт именно Dev.
explanation.uk: В абзаці G Dev Sandoval радить кандидатам чесно сказати, що вони зробили б зараз інакше. Запитання ставить Owen, але цю пораду дає саме Dev.

questions.prompt: Every candidate is asked to talk about a time when things did not go as planned.
questions.evidence: He asks every candidate to describe a real occasion when a plan fell apart

explanation.en: Paragraph G says Owen Kariuki leads the final interview and asks every candidate about a time a plan fell apart.
explanation.ru: В абзаце G сказано, что Owen Kariuki проводит финальное собеседование и просит каждого кандидата рассказать о случае, когда план провалился.
explanation.uk: В абзаці G сказано, що Owen Kariuki проводить фінальну співбесіду і просить кожного кандидата розповісти про випадок, коли план провалився.

groups.instruction: Look at the following statements and the list of people below. Match each statement with the correct person, A–E. You may use any letter more than once.

sections.text:
The Long Road to Your Teacup

A. Tea is now drunk in almost every country, yet few drinkers give much thought to how it is made. Whether it arrives as a delicate pale green brew in a Japanese bowl or as a strong, milky mug in a British kitchen, almost every cup of tea in the world begins in the same place: the leaves of a single evergreen shrub, Camellia sinensis. Herbal infusions such as peppermint or chamomile are often called tea, but strictly speaking they are something else. Black, green, oolong and white teas are not made from different plants, as many drinkers assume. What separates them is what happens to the leaves in the hours and days after they are picked, and those changes begin long before any kettle is switched on.

B. Left alone, a tea plant would grow into a small tree several metres tall. On plantations, however, the bushes are pruned to roughly waist height, creating a flat, dense surface that growers call the plucking table. In the growing season, new shoots appear on this surface every week or two, and these are what the pickers are after. The traditional rule is 'two leaves and a bud': only the tender tip of each shoot is taken. Sabitha Moorcroft, who manages a hillside tea garden, says that experienced pluckers can gather many kilograms a day without slowing down. 'Machines are quicker and cheaper,' she admits, 'but they can't tell a fresh shoot from a tough old leaf, so they take both. For our better teas, nothing replaces a trained pair of hands.'

C. For most teas, once the baskets reach the factory, the leaves are spread out in long troughs, and warm air is blown through them for many hours. This stage, known as withering, removes a good deal of their moisture and turns the leaves soft and floppy, rather like spinach left out of the fridge. Soft leaves can then be rolled without snapping. Rolling, done by hand on small estates and by machine on large ones, twists the leaves and breaks open their cells, so that the juices inside come into contact with the air. It looks like a simple mechanical step, but it sets off the chemistry that gives each tea its character.

D. That chemistry is oxidation, a process often wrongly called fermentation. Enzymes in the bruised leaf react with oxygen, and the leaves gradually darken, much as a cut apple turns brown on a kitchen counter. Allowed to continue for an hour or more, the reaction produces the coppery colour and full, malty flavour of black tea. Oolong makers stop the process partway, which is why oolongs range from almost green to nearly black. Green tea is heated soon after picking, by steaming or pan-firing, so the enzymes are destroyed before they can do their work and the leaves keep their colour and fresh, grassy taste. White tea is handled least of all: it is simply withered and dried. Whatever the style, the leaves finish with a final drying, which brings their moisture so low that they will keep for months.

E. Before tea reaches the shops, it passes through the hands, and mouths, of professional tasters. Haruto Ebdon spends his mornings in a tasting room where dozens of white bowls stand in a row, each holding a sample from a different estate. He slurps every spoonful noisily, a habit that startles visitors but sprays the tea across the palate so that no flavour is missed. His main job is blending. A single garden's tea changes with the weather and the season, yet customers expect their favourite brand to taste the same every time they buy it. Blending is sometimes suspected of being a way to hide cheap leaf, but Ebdon insists that consistency is the real aim: 'I might combine twenty teas from four countries just so that this year's packet tastes exactly like last year's.' Long before this, at the factory, the leaves will have been sorted by size: whole leaves are sold loose, while the smallest broken pieces, which release their flavour quickly, mostly end up in tea bags.

F. The final stage of the journey takes place in our own kitchens, and it is the one we most often get wrong. Black tea generally suits water straight off the boil, but more delicate teas do not, and green and white teas in particular can turn bitter if the water is too hot. In one study, the food scientist Clémence Adjei asked volunteers to compare cups of the same green tea brewed at different temperatures without telling them which was which. Most preferred the cup made with water at around 80°C, and many described the boiling-water version as harsh and bitter. Adjei admits her study was small, involving only twenty-four volunteers, but her advice is easy to follow: let the kettle stand for a few minutes before pouring. After so many skilled hands have shaped the leaf, it seems a pity to ruin it in the last thirty seconds.

options.text: One plant, many teas
A careful harvest of the newest growth
Softening and breaking the leaf
How exposure to air shapes colour and flavour
Experts who keep a familiar taste the same
The final step happens in the kitchen
Why machines are replacing human pickers

questions.prompt: Paragraph A
questions.evidence: Black, green, oolong and white teas are not made from different plants

explanation.en: Paragraph A explains that all true teas come from one shrub and differ only because of how the leaves are processed. It mentions different countries, but it does not describe how tea spread around the world.
explanation.ru: В абзаце A объясняется, что весь настоящий чай получают с одного кустарника, а различается он только тем, как обрабатывают листья. Там упоминаются разные страны, но не описывается, как чай распространился по миру.
explanation.uk: В абзаці A пояснюється, що весь справжній чай походить з одного куща, а відрізняється лише тим, як обробляють листя. Там згадано різні країни, але не описано, як чай поширився світом.

questions.prompt: Paragraph B
questions.evidence: The traditional rule is 'two leaves and a bud': only the tender tip of each shoot is taken.

explanation.en: Paragraph B is about picking only the young shoots from the bushes. Machines are mentioned, but Moorcroft says hand-picking is still needed for better teas, so the paragraph is not about machines replacing people.
explanation.ru: Абзац B посвящён сбору только молодых побегов с кустов. Машины там упоминаются, но Moorcroft говорит, что для более качественного чая по-прежнему нужен ручной сбор, так что абзац не о том, что машины заменяют людей.
explanation.uk: Абзац B присвячений збиранню лише молодих пагонів із кущів. Машини там згадано, але Moorcroft каже, що для якіснішого чаю досі потрібне ручне збирання, тож абзац не про те, що машини замінюють людей.

questions.prompt: Paragraph C
questions.evidence: Rolling, done by hand on small estates and by machine on large ones, twists the leaves and breaks open their cells

explanation.en: Paragraph C describes withering, which makes the leaves soft, and rolling, which breaks open their cells. Both steps together match the idea of softening and breaking the leaf.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C описаны завяливание («withering»), которое делает листья мягкими, и скручивание («rolling»), которое разрушает их клетки. Вместе эти два этапа соответствуют идее размягчения и разрушения листа.
explanation.uk: В абзаці C описано в'ялення («withering»), яке робить листя м'яким, і скручування («rolling»), яке руйнує його клітини. Разом ці два етапи відповідають ідеї розм'якшення та руйнування листка.

questions.prompt: Paragraph D
questions.evidence: Enzymes in the bruised leaf react with oxygen, and the leaves gradually darken

explanation.en: Paragraph D explains oxidation, a reaction with oxygen, and shows how stopping it early or late gives green, oolong or black tea with different colours and tastes.
explanation.ru: В абзаце D объясняется окисление («oxidation») — реакция с кислородом — и показано, как ранняя или поздняя его остановка даёт зелёный чай, улун или чёрный чай с разным цветом и вкусом.
explanation.uk: В абзаці D пояснюється окиснення («oxidation») — реакція з киснем — і показано, як рання або пізня його зупинка дає зелений чай, улун або чорний чай із різним кольором і смаком.

questions.prompt: Paragraph E
questions.evidence: customers expect their favourite brand to taste the same every time they buy it

explanation.en: Paragraph E is about professional tasters like Ebdon, whose main job is blending teas so a brand always tastes the same. Sorting leaves by size is only a small detail.
explanation.ru: Абзац E посвящён профессиональным дегустаторам, таким как Ebdon, главная задача которых — смешивать чаи так, чтобы у марки всегда был одинаковый вкус. Сортировка листьев по размеру — лишь небольшая деталь.
explanation.uk: Абзац E присвячений професійним дегустаторам, як-от Ebdon, головне завдання яких — змішувати чаї так, щоб марка завжди мала однаковий смак. Сортування листя за розміром — лише дрібна деталь.

questions.prompt: Paragraph F
questions.evidence: The final stage of the journey takes place in our own kitchens, and it is the one we most often get wrong.

explanation.en: Paragraph F is about brewing tea at home, especially choosing the right water temperature. It mentions green tea, but it says nothing about health benefits.
explanation.ru: Абзац F о заваривании чая дома, особенно о выборе правильной температуры воды. Зелёный чай там упоминается, но о пользе для здоровья ничего не сказано.
explanation.uk: Абзац F про заварювання чаю вдома, особливо про вибір правильної температури води. Зелений чай там згадано, але про користь для здоров'я нічого не сказано.

groups.instruction: The passage has six paragraphs, A–F. Choose the correct heading for each paragraph from the list of headings below. Write the correct number, i–ix. There are more headings than paragraphs, so you will not use them all.

questions.prompt: On plantations, tea bushes are cut back so that their tops form a level surface known as the ______.
questions.evidence: creating a flat, dense surface that growers call the plucking table

explanation.en: Paragraph B says the bushes are pruned to waist height, creating a flat surface that growers call the plucking table. 'Cut back' restates 'pruned'.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B говорится, что кусты подрезают до уровня пояса, и получается ровная поверхность, которую чаеводы называют «plucking table». «Cut back» — это перефразирование слова «pruned».
explanation.uk: В абзаці B ідеться про те, що кущі підрізають до рівня пояса, і утворюється рівна поверхня, яку чаярі називають «plucking table». «Cut back» — це перефразування слова «pruned».

questions.prompt: During withering, the leaves lose much of their moisture while ______ is passed through them for hours.
questions.evidence: warm air is blown through them for many hours

explanation.en: Paragraph C says warm air is blown through the leaves for many hours, and this stage, withering, removes much of their moisture.
explanation.ru: В абзаце C сказано, что через листья много часов продувают тёплый воздух, и этот этап — «withering» — удаляет бо́льшую часть их влаги.
explanation.uk: В абзаці C сказано, що крізь листя багато годин продувають тепле повітря, і цей етап — «withering» — видаляє значну частину їхньої вологи.

questions.prompt: The process of oxidation is frequently given the incorrect name ______.
questions.evidence: a process often wrongly called fermentation

explanation.en: Paragraph D says oxidation is 'often wrongly called fermentation'. 'Frequently given the incorrect name' restates this.
explanation.ru: В абзаце D говорится, что окисление «often wrongly called fermentation». Фраза «frequently given the incorrect name» передаёт ту же мысль другими словами.
explanation.uk: В абзаці D ідеться про те, що окиснення «often wrongly called fermentation». Фраза «frequently given the incorrect name» передає ту саму думку іншими словами.

questions.prompt: Ebdon's noisy slurping spreads each sample of tea across his ______.
questions.evidence: sprays the tea across the palate so that no flavour is missed

explanation.en: Paragraph E says slurping sprays the tea across the palate, so that the taster does not miss any flavour.
explanation.ru: В абзаце E сказано, что когда чай шумно втягивают («slurping»), он распыляется по всему нёбу («palate»), и дегустатор не упускает ни одного оттенка вкуса («flavour»).
explanation.uk: В абзаці E сказано, що коли чай гучно втягують («slurping»), він розпорошується по всьому піднебінню («palate»), і дегустатор не пропускає жодного відтінку смаку («flavour»).

groups.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.

options.text: gathers older leaves as well as new shoots.
damages the flat surface of the bushes.
is slower than an experienced plucker.
costs more than employing trained pickers.

questions.prompt: According to Sabitha Moorcroft, the main drawback of harvesting tea by machine is that it
questions.evidence: they can't tell a fresh shoot from a tough old leaf, so they take both

explanation.en: In paragraph B, Moorcroft says machines cannot tell fresh shoots from old leaves and take both. She says machines are quicker and cheaper, so the options about cost and speed are wrong, and she never mentions damage to the bushes.
explanation.ru: В абзаце B Moorcroft говорит, что машины не могут отличить свежие побеги от старых листьев и срывают и то и другое. По её словам, машины быстрее и дешевле, поэтому варианты о стоимости и скорости неверны, а о повреждении кустов она вообще не упоминает.
explanation.uk: В абзаці B Moorcroft каже, що машини не можуть відрізнити свіжі пагони від старого листя і зривають і те, і інше. За її словами, машини швидші й дешевші, тому варіанти про вартість і швидкість неправильні, а про пошкодження кущів вона взагалі не згадує.

groups.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

options.text: to reduce their moisture for long storage
to prevent their reaction with oxygen
to make them soft enough to be rolled
to give them a coppery colour and flavour

questions.prompt: Why are green tea leaves heated soon after they are picked?
questions.evidence: so the enzymes are destroyed before they can do their work and the leaves keep their colour

explanation.en: Paragraph D says heating destroys the enzymes before oxidation, the reaction with oxygen, can happen. Softening comes from withering, the final drying for storage applies to all teas, and the coppery colour belongs to black tea.
explanation.ru: В абзаце D сказано, что нагревание разрушает ферменты до того, как может начаться окисление — реакция с кислородом. Размягчение происходит при завяливании, окончательная сушка для хранения применяется ко всем чаям, а медный цвет характерен для чёрного чая.
explanation.uk: В абзаці D сказано, що нагрівання руйнує ферменти ще до того, як може початися окиснення — реакція з киснем. Розм'якшення відбувається під час в'ялення, остаточне сушіння для зберігання стосується всіх чаїв, а мідний колір властивий чорному чаю.

groups.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

options.text: to include teas from as many countries as possible
to disguise poorer leaf from some estates
to keep a product's flavour unchanged over time
to produce a new taste for each season

questions.prompt: What does Haruto Ebdon say is the purpose of blending tea?
questions.evidence: just so that this year's packet tastes exactly like last year's

explanation.en: In paragraph E, Ebdon says consistency is the real aim, so that this year's tea tastes like last year's. Hiding cheap leaf is only what some people suspect, and he mentions four countries as an example, not as a goal.
explanation.ru: В абзаце E Ebdon говорит, что настоящая цель — постоянство: чтобы чай этого года был на вкус таким же, как прошлогодний. Сокрытие дешёвого листа — лишь то, что подозревают некоторые, а четыре страны он упоминает как пример, а не как цель.
explanation.uk: В абзаці E Ebdon каже, що справжня мета — сталість: щоб цьогорічний чай смакував так само, як торішній. Приховування дешевого листя — лише те, що дехто підозрює, а чотири країни він згадує як приклад, а не як мету.
